newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal bond auction seen near secondary market.
newsitem.headline: Portugal bond auction seen near secondary market.

text.p: Bids at today's auction of three-year Portuguese bonds will be near the secondary market level, but the large yield spreads against three-year Bonos could cut bids to below 5.80 percent, dealers said.
"Today's auction of March 1999 fixed rate bonds has the secondary market as its reference and is likely to come out between 5.80 and 5.85 percent," a fixed rate director said.
An analyst with an investment bank said: "The large, positive yield spread against three-year Bonos could justify bids coming in below the psychological barrier of 5.80 percent."
Results of today's auction of 20 billion escudos of three-year Treasury Bonds are due around 1100 GMT.
At the last similar auction on December 10, 16.6 billion escudos of three-year bonds were placed at an average weighted interest rate of 6.0718 percent.
Yesterday March 1999 bonds closed at 10,534 escudos to yield 5.82 percent with a yield spread of 18 basis points over April 1999 Bonos.
